conclusion: Hot-expert kernels stream on persistent grids (the decode MoE expert pipeline is 13-16% faster at width 4 and 6-11% at width 1, bit-identical), the combine's CPU-tier wait overlaps hot_down, the GR norm/down kernel preloads its inject rows and row scales, and the verify step's GDN/PLE folds run beside the MTP drafts. Coding chat decodes 3.5% / 9.3% more tokens per second with 7-8% less time per speculative round; corpus decode changes are within run-to-run noise except the 32K prompt.

baseline.description: Frozen round-six baseline build (tree after the fifth pass)

runtime_changes: hot_gate_up: persistent grid (CTAs per SM from the occupancy API) over (item, 8-row) tiles; one tile buffer streamed in five K slices, slice i - 1 of the next tile requested as soon as slice i of the current one is decoded
hot_down: persistent grid over (item, 32-row) tiles in contiguous ranges, two cp.async stages, h quantized to q8 once per item per CTA; triggers its dependent first thing
combine: the CPU-tier wait (done[l]) and the PCIe read of the CPU result run before pdl_wait, beside hot_down; the ablation direction is loaded first
gr_norm_down: inject rows (cluster 0) and down row scales (rank 0) load before pdl_wait
verify steps with MTP drafts: the GDN fold (64-CTA swept grid) and the PLE fold run on the prefetch stream beside the drafts, joined at the end of the step
test_changes: kernels_moe_experts --bench: width-4 decode case (28 experts, 40 pairs) and select timings with and without a host exchange
kernels_gdn_fold: the in-place fold also by a 37-CTA swept grid, bit-exact against the reference

method.order: baseline then current per round, separate processes
method.note: End-to-end runs include adaptive expert placement and the speculation controller, whose width choice follows measured step latencies; both vary between processes.

moe_decode_select_gate_up_down_combine_u.method: kernels_moe_experts --bench-only: 16 steps per graph (working set beyond L2), min of 300 replays; width 1 = 10 experts, width 4 = 28 experts / 40 pairs; baseline and current test binaries back to back

gr_read_pair_us.method: gr_norm_down + GR up (GrMix) in a 32-call graph, min of 100 replays (scratch harness against the built libraries)

verify_step_tail_nsys_median_us.method: nsys coding chat, width-4 verify graph, same session state for both builds

fidelity.decode_path_vs_baseline: fngine-validate --decode-width W --no-adaptive --expert-vram-mib 22000 --compare-logits: G1 W=1, G1 W=4 and G2 W=4 top-1 agreement 1.0, mean and max KLD 0

rejected_experiments.result: Decode-latency bound: width-4 gate/up 30.2 -> 37.8 us; compute alone 5.5 -> 20.6 us

rejected_experiments.experiment: Uniform slice windows of 1-3 slices for the streaming gate/up
rejected_experiments.result: Width 4 slower than the eager refill (28.5 vs 29.2-30.1 us); width 1 mixed

Batched h quantization alone in the one-tile-per-CTA down kernel
rejected_experiments.result: Unchanged (29.4 us at width 4): the kernel was bound by synchronized waves, not by the quantization
